q: Stores whose shelf life has expired while lying in a stores depot:

options.A: Are issued on priority for immediate use
options.B: Are sold to railway employees at the book rate
options.C: Are re-tested and their shelf life extended by the depot officer
options.D: Cannot be issued for use and are dealt with as unserviceable stores, to be surveyed off

e: Stores whose shelf life has expired cannot be certified fit for use, so they cannot be issued and are dealt with as unserviceable stores, to be surveyed off.

q: The AAC of an item is 8,400 units. The stock in hand is 1,100 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 300 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Monthly consumption = 8,400 / 12 = 700 units; coverage = (stock in hand 1,100 + dues 300) / 700 = 2 months.

q: The stock verifiers who carry out the physical verification of stores in depots function under the:

options.A: Stores Department, headed by the Principal Chief Materials Manager
options.B: Accounts Department, in the FA&CAO's organisation
options.C: Operating Department of the zonal railway

e: Stock verifiers function under the Accounts Department in the FA&CAO's organisation, so that physical verification of stores remains independent of the Stores Department holding their custody.

q: A supplier fails to supply 600 units of stores contracted at Rs 75 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 90 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost of risk purchase = (Rs 90 - Rs 75) x 600 units = Rs 9,000, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: Every stores item is accounted for in the priced accounts of a depot in:

options.A: The unit (number, kilogram, metre, etc.) prescribed for the item in the priced list
options.B: Rupees only, without reference to quantity
options.C: Tonnes, whatever be the nature of the item
options.D: Dozens, for the sake of uniformity

e: Every stores item is accounted for in the unit (number, kilogram, metre, etc.) prescribed for it in the priced list, so that quantity and value accounts remain linked item-wise.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,600 units. The average consumption is 90 units per week and the average lead time is 10 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum level = re-order level - (average consumption x average lead time) = 1,600 - (90 x 10) = 700 units.

q: In ABC analysis of stores inventory, 'A' category items are generally characterised by:

options.A: A large proportion of the total number of items accounting for a small part of the consumption value
options.B: A small proportion of the total number of items (about 10 per cent) accounting for a large proportion (about 70 per cent) of the annual consumption value
options.C: Items which are consumed only in workshops
options.D: Items whose unit rate is the highest among all stores items

e: In ABC analysis, 'A' category items are a small proportion (about 10 per cent) of the total items but account for a large proportion (about 70 per cent) of the annual consumption value, hence their tight control.

q: Six wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 2 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 1,200 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Total demurrage = 6 wagons x 2 days x Rs 1,200 per wagon per day = Rs 14,400 for detention beyond the free time.

q: Under the price variation clause of a stores contract, the price payable for the stores may:

options.A: Increase or decrease, according to the movement of the indices/formula stipulated in the contract
options.D: Change only with the prior approval of the Railway Board in each case

e: Under the price variation clause, the price payable adjusts according to the indices/formula stipulated in the contract, so it may increase or decrease with the movement of those indices.

q: The re-order level of an item is 2,400 units and the re-order quantity is 1,500 units. The minimum consumption is 70 units per week and the minimum lead time is 6 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 2,400 + 1,500 - (70 x 6) = 3,480 units.

q: For submitting an e-tender for stores on IREPS, a firm is required to have:

options.A: A seller registration on the GeM portal only
options.C: A bank guarantee from a nationalised bank
options.D: An ISO certification for its products

e: For submitting an e-tender on IREPS, a firm must have a valid Digital Signature Certificate, since bids are signed and submitted electronically.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 200 units per week, its normal consumption is 160 units per week and the lead time is 4 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item is:
e: Safety stock = (maximum consumption - normal consumption) x lead time = (200 - 160) x 4 = 160 units.

q: Physical verification of stores in a depot is carried out by the stock verifier:

options.A: In the presence of the stockholder (custodian) or his authorised representative
options.B: Only from the bin cards, without opening the bins
options.C: In the absence of all depot staff
options.D: Only for items selected by the stockholder

e: Physical verification is carried out in the presence of the stockholder or his authorised representative, so that differences found are seen and acknowledged at the time of verification itself.

q: The average consumption of an item is 65 units per week, the lead time is 7 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock is 180 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = average consumption x lead time + safety stock = 65 x 7 + 180 = 635 units.

q: Where a material change is made in the conditions of a stores tender after the tender notice has been issued, the change is brought to the notice of the tenderers through:

options.A: A letter sent only to the lowest tenderer
options.B: A corrigendum to the tender notice, with suitable extension of the due date where necessary
options.C: An announcement made at the time of opening of the tenders
options.D: A fresh registration of the tenderers

e: A material change in tender conditions after the notice is issued is notified to all tenderers through a corrigendum to the tender notice, with extension of the due date where necessary.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 3,600 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 100 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 8 per unit per year. The total of the ordering cost and the carrying cost per year, when orders are placed in Economic Order Quantities, is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x 3,600 x 100 / 8) = 300 units, giving 12 orders; ordering cost = 12 x Rs 100 = Rs 1,200 and carrying cost = (300/2) x Rs 8 = Rs 1,200, total Rs 2,400, the two being equal at EOQ.

q: In e-tendering for stores through IREPS, a bid sought to be submitted after the due date and time:

options.A: Cannot be submitted, as the system automatically closes bid submission at the stipulated time
options.B: Is accepted on payment of a late fee by the tenderer
options.C: Is accepted with the approval of the Tender Committee
options.D: Is treated as an unsolicited offer and kept pending

e: In IREPS e-tendering the system automatically closes bid submission at the stipulated due date and time, so a bid sought to be submitted late cannot be submitted at all.

q: The minimum level of an item is 900 units and the maximum level is 3,100 units. The average stock level of the item is:
e: Average stock level = (minimum level + maximum level) / 2 = (900 + 3,100) / 2 = 2,000 units.

q: Under the IRS Conditions of Contract, disputes between the Railway and a supplier in connection with a stores contract, which cannot be settled mutually, are referred to arbitration, and the arbitrator is appointed by:

options.B: The General Manager of the Railway
options.C: The District Court of the place of supply

e: Under the IRS Conditions of Contract, disputes not settled mutually are referred to arbitration, and the arbitrator is appointed by the General Manager of the Railway.

q: The total issues of stores of a railway during a year are Rs 3.6 crore and the average stock held is Rs 60 lakh. The stock of stores turns over, i.e. the inventory turnover, during the year is:
e: Inventory turnover = total issues / average stock = Rs 3.6 crore / Rs 60 lakh = 6 times during the year.

q: For an item which is to be stocked in a depot for the first time, its AAC (Average Annual Consumption) is fixed on the basis of:

options.A: The anticipated requirement of the item assessed by the user department, there being no past consumption of the item
options.B: The AAC of a similar item stocked on another railway
options.C: The maximum stock level prescribed for the depot
options.D: The quantity covered by the first purchase order placed for the item

e: For an item stocked for the first time there is no past consumption, so its AAC is fixed on the basis of the anticipated requirement assessed by the user department.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 12 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 45 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 50 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:

options.A: A debit balance of Rs 17 lakh
options.B: A credit balance of Rs 7 lakh
options.C: A debit balance of Rs 5 lakh
options.D: A debit balance of Rs 7 lakh

e: Purchase Suspense: opening debit Rs 12 lakh + bills paid Rs 45 lakh - material received and linked Rs 50 lakh = closing debit balance of Rs 7 lakh.

q: Other things remaining the same, if the annual consumption of a stores item doubles, its Economic Order Quantity will:

options.B: Increase by about 41 per cent, i.e. in the ratio of the square root of two, and not double

e: EOQ varies with the square root of annual consumption, so doubling consumption increases EOQ only in the ratio of square root of 2, i.e. by about 41 per cent, and does not double it.

q: Scrap having a book value of Rs 50,000 is sold by e-auction for Rs 68,000. The excess of the sale value over the book value, amounting to Rs 18,000, is:

options.B: Treated as a miscellaneous receipt of the Stores Department
options.C: Credited to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: Adjusted against the security deposit of the purchaser

e: Scrap sold for Rs 68,000 against a book value of Rs 50,000 yields an excess of Rs 18,000, which is credited to the Stock Adjustment Account, not treated as departmental earnings.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 6,300 units and the quantity ordered each time (Economic Order Quantity) is 700 units. The number of orders to be placed during the year is:
e: Number of orders = annual requirement / EOQ = 6,300 / 700 = 9 orders in the year.

q:
Consider the following statements about purchases through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), as per the General Financial Rules:
1. For purchases above Rs 25,000 and up to Rs 5 lakh, the buyer compares the offerings of at least three sellers/brands available on GeM and purchases from the lowest (L1) among them.
2. For purchases above Rs 25,000, direct purchase without any price comparison is permitted on GeM.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Under GFR Rule 149 as amended, GeM direct purchase without comparison is allowed up to Rs 50,000; above Rs 50,000 up to Rs 10 lakh purchase is through the lowest-priced seller among at least three manufacturers; above Rs 10 lakh, online bidding/reverse auction is mandatory. (Source: Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, GFR amendment dated 10.07.2024.)

q: Where an item available on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is proposed to be procured from outside GeM, the buyer is required, before doing so, to generate on the GeM portal the:

options.C: GeM Availability Report and Past Transaction Summary (GeMARPTS) ID
options.D: Stock sheet of the depot holding the item

e: Before buying outside GeM an item available on it, the buyer must generate the GeM Availability Report and Past Transaction Summary (GeMARPTS) ID on the portal, recording that GeM was checked first.

q: Depreciation is NOT charged on:

options.A: Plant and machinery installed in workshops
options.B: Stores held in stock in depots, which are current assets valued at book (cost) value
options.C: Rolling stock owned by the Railways
options.D: Buildings and structures of the Railways

e: Depreciation is charged on fixed assets, not on stores held in stock, which are current assets valued at book (cost) value until issued.

q: In the two-packet (two-bid) system of stores tendering, the Earnest Money Deposit is required to be submitted by the tenderer:

options.B: After the tender has been accepted
options.C: Along with the Security Deposit, after placement of the order
options.D: Along with the techno-commercial bid (the first packet)

e: In the two-packet system, the Earnest Money Deposit is submitted along with the techno-commercial bid (the first packet), so that only bids secured by earnest money are evaluated before prices are opened.

q: Where cent per cent inspection of every unit of a large lot of stores is impracticable, inspection is carried out:

options.A: On the basis of samples drawn as prescribed, the lot being accepted or rejected on the results of the sample inspection
options.B: By inspecting only the top layer of the packages in the lot
options.C: By accepting the supplier's own test certificate in all cases
options.D: Only after the stores have been put into use

e: Where cent per cent inspection is impracticable, inspection is done on samples drawn as prescribed, and the lot is accepted or rejected on the results of the sample inspection.

q: The coverage (in months) prescribed for high-value 'A' category stores items is generally kept lower than that prescribed for low-value 'C' category items, mainly in order to:

options.A: Increase the stock of 'A' category items held in depots
options.B: Ensure that 'A' category items are purchased more frequently at higher rates
options.C: Limit the capital locked up in high-value stock
options.D: Reduce the number of purchase orders placed for 'C' category items

e: Coverage for high-value 'A' category items is kept lower mainly to limit the capital locked up in high-value stock held in depots.

q: The head of the stores organisation at the headquarters of a zonal railway, who was earlier designated as the Controller of Stores, is now designated as the:
e: The head of the stores organisation at zonal railway headquarters, earlier designated Controller of Stores, is now designated as the Principal Chief Materials Manager.

q:
Consider the following statements about stores imported on 'F.O.B.' (Free On Board) terms:
1. The marine insurance of the consignment for the sea transit is arranged by the Railway, as buyer, since the price does not cover insurance beyond the port of shipment.
2. A claim for loss or damage to the consignment during the sea transit is preferred by the Railway on the insurer under the marine policy.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: on FOB terms the price excludes insurance beyond the port of shipment, so the Railway as buyer arranges the marine insurance and prefers transit claims on the insurer under that policy.

q: Stores covered by a Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC) are purchased from:

options.A: The proprietary firm (original equipment manufacturer) or its authorised dealer/agent
options.B: Any firm quoting the lowest rate in an open tender

e: Stores covered by a Proprietary Article Certificate are proprietary in nature and can be purchased only from the proprietary firm (original equipment manufacturer) or its authorised dealer/agent.

q:
Consider the following statements about stores accounting in the General Books:
1. Issues of stores from depots are credited to the Stores Suspense (stock) account, the head of account of the consuming department or work being debited with their value.
2. Issues of stores from depots are debited to the Purchase Suspense account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: issues from depots are credited to the Stores Suspense (stock) account with the consuming head debited. Statement 2 is wrong, as Purchase Suspense records purchases and bills, not issues.

q:
Consider the following statements about stores rejected on inspection at a depot:
1. The cost of returning the rejected stores to the supplier is borne by the Railway.
2. The rejected stores are removed by the supplier at his own cost within the period stipulated in the contract.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 2 only is correct: rejected stores are removed by the supplier at his own cost within the stipulated period; the cost of returning them is not borne by the Railway, so statement 1 is false.

q: The blank Receipt Note and Issue Note books held in a stores depot are:

options.A: Ordinary stationery requiring no special custody
options.B: Supplied to the depot by the firms supplying stores
options.C: Maintained only in electronic form, with no physical books
options.D: Treated as accountable (money-value) forms, kept in safe custody with their use properly accounted for

e: Blank Receipt Note and Issue Note books are treated as accountable (money-value) forms, kept in safe custody with their use properly accounted for, since they can create or move stock value.

q:
Consider the following statements about purchases through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM):
1. The Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate (CRAC) is generated by the consignee after the goods have been received and accepted.
2. Payment to the GeM seller is released only after the CRAC has been generated.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the consignee generates the CRAC after the goods are received and accepted, and payment to the GeM seller is released only after the CRAC has been generated.

q: In the e-auction of scrap conducted on IREPS, each successive bid for a lot must:

options.A: Be equal to the reserve price of the lot
options.B: Exceed the previous highest bid at least by the bid increment specified for the lot
options.C: Be accompanied by a fresh earnest money deposit
options.D: Be approved in advance by the Tender Committee

e: In the IREPS e-auction of scrap, each successive bid must exceed the previous highest bid at least by the bid increment specified for the lot.

q:
Consider the following statements about differences found in stock verification:
1. A shortage of an item found in one ward of a depot cannot be set off against an excess of the same item found in another ward; each difference is brought on record and adjusted separately through its own stock sheet.
2. Only the net difference of an item, after setting off all shortages and excesses in the depot, is adjusted in the accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: a shortage in one ward cannot be set off against an excess of the same item in another ward; each difference is recorded and adjusted separately through its own stock sheet, so netting (statement 2) is not allowed.

q: High Speed Diesel (HSD) oil required for diesel locomotives is stocked in, and issued from, fuel installations of the Railways known as:

options.B: Imprest stores held by loco pilots
options.C: Oil sidings of the Traffic Department

e: High Speed Diesel oil for diesel locomotives is stocked in, and issued from, the Railway Consumer Depots (RCDs), the dedicated fuel installations of the Railways.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 5,000 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 50 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 8 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual consumption x ordering cost / carrying cost) = square root of (2 x 5,000 x 50 / 8) = 250 units.

q: A depot holds 800 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 25 per unit. A fresh receipt of 400 units is taken into stock at Rs 40 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Revised average rate = (800 x Rs 25 + 400 x Rs 40) / 1,200 units = Rs 36,000 / 1,200 = Rs 30 per unit.

q: A stores depot issues 725 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 36 per unit. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
e: Issue value = 725 units x Rs 36 per unit = Rs 26,100, debited to the consuming department at the book rate.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 18 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 450 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Shortage value = 18 units x Rs 450 per unit = Rs 8,100, the shortage being valued at the book rate.

q: During stock verification, 24 units of an item are found in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 125 per unit. The value of the excess taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account is:
e: Excess value = 24 units x Rs 125 per unit = Rs 3,000, taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 3,50,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 7 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: Liquidated damages = 0.5 per cent of Rs 3,50,000 = Rs 1,750 per week x 7 weeks = Rs 12,250.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 9,25,000. The advance payment admissible at 98 per cent of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment = 98 per cent of Rs 9,25,000 = Rs 9,06,500, admissible against the inspection certificate and despatch documents.

q: A supplier fails to supply 350 units of stores contracted at Rs 60 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 78 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost of risk purchase = (Rs 78 - Rs 60) x 350 units = Rs 6,300, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: Seven wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 3 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 800 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Total demurrage = 7 wagons x 3 days x Rs 800 per wagon per day = Rs 16,800 for detention beyond the free time.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 65 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 2.75 crore and issues during the year are Rs 2.6 crore. The closing balance of stores is:
e: Closing balance = opening Rs 65 lakh + receipts Rs 2.75 crore - issues Rs 2.6 crore = Rs 80 lakh.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 55 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 2.5 crore. The Turnover Ratio of stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance / total issues = Rs 55 lakh / Rs 2.5 crore = 0.22.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 2.3 crore and the closing balance is Rs 1.7 crore. The average stock held during the year is:
e: Average stock = (opening balance Rs 2.3 crore + closing balance Rs 1.7 crore) / 2 = Rs 2.0 crore.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 2.5 crore. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 12 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Annual carrying cost = 12 per cent of the average stock value of Rs 2.5 crore = Rs 30 lakh.

q: The AAC of an item is 6,600 units. The stock in hand is 1,200 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 450 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Monthly consumption = 6,600 / 12 = 550 units; coverage = (stock in hand 1,200 + dues 450) / 550 = 3 months.

q: The AAC of an item is 7,500 units. Coverage for four months is required to be provided. The stock in hand is 900 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 600 units. The quantity to be ordered is:
e: Four months' requirement = 7,500 x 4/12 = 2,500 units; quantity to order = 2,500 - stock in hand 900 - dues 600 = 1,000 units.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 90 units per week, its normal consumption is 70 units per week and the lead time is 6 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item is:
e: Safety stock = (maximum consumption - normal consumption) x lead time = (90 - 70) x 6 = 120 units.

q: The re-order level of an item is 2,200 units. The average consumption is 130 units per week and the average lead time is 10 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum level = re-order level - (average consumption x average lead time) = 2,200 - (130 x 10) = 900 units.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,750 units and the re-order quantity is 1,100 units. The minimum consumption is 55 units per week and the minimum lead time is 5 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1,750 + 1,100 - (55 x 5) = 2,575 units.

q: The minimum level of an item is 750 units and the maximum level is 2,850 units. The average stock level of the item is:
e: Average stock level = (minimum level + maximum level) / 2 = (750 + 2,850) / 2 = 1,800 units.

q: The average consumption of an item is 55 units per day, the lead time for its procurement is 12 days and the safety (buffer) stock is 240 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = average consumption x lead time + safety stock = 55 x 12 + 240 = 900 units.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 8,400 units and the quantity ordered each time (Economic Order Quantity) is 600 units. The number of orders to be placed during the year is:
e: Number of orders = annual requirement / EOQ = 8,400 / 600 = 14 orders in the year.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 20 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 55 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 48 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:
e: Purchase Suspense: opening debit Rs 20 lakh + bills paid Rs 55 lakh - material received and linked Rs 48 lakh = closing debit balance of Rs 27 lakh.

q: A depot holds 2,400 units of an item. The book rate of the item is revised from Rs 85 to Rs 78 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Decrease in stock value = 2,400 units x (Rs 85 - Rs 78) = Rs 16,800, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account on the downward revision of the book rate.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 2,750 units and its book rate is Rs 160 per unit. For the purposes of ABC analysis, the annual consumption value of the item is:
e: Annual consumption value = 2,750 units x Rs 160 = Rs 4,40,000; ABC classification is based on this consumption value.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 10,800 units and its Economic Order Quantity is 900 units. If the cost of placing one order is Rs 250, the total ordering cost per year is:
e: Orders per year = 10,800 / 900 = 12; total ordering cost = 12 x Rs 250 = Rs 3,000.

q: The total issues of stores of a railway during a year are Rs 5.6 crore and the average stock held is Rs 80 lakh. The inventory turnover of the stores during the year is:
e: Inventory turnover = total issues / average stock = Rs 5.6 crore / Rs 80 lakh = 7 times during the year.

q: The average consumption of an item is 175 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 4 weeks. The consumption of the item during the lead time is:
e: Lead-time consumption = average consumption x lead time = 175 units per week x 4 weeks = 700 units.

q: An item has an Economic Order Quantity of 1,100 units and a safety stock of 200 units. Under the EOQ system with a uniform rate of consumption, the average inventory of the item held is:
e: Average inventory = EOQ/2 + safety stock = 550 + 200 = 750 units, since with uniform consumption the cycle stock averages half the order quantity.

q: The safety (buffer) stock of an item is 320 units and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 15 per unit per year. The annual carrying cost attributable to the safety stock is:
e: Annual carrying cost of safety stock = 320 units x Rs 15 per unit = Rs 4,800.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Railway Stores Code is issued in two volumes.
2. Volume I of the Stores Code deals mainly with the purchase of stores, while Volume II deals with depot working, custody and accounts of stores.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Indian Railway Stores Code is issued in two volumes, Volume I dealing mainly with purchase of stores and Volume II with depot working, custody and accounts of stores.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 3,200 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 200 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 2 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual consumption x ordering cost / carrying cost) = square root of (2 x 3,200 x 200 / 2) = 800 units.

q: On the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), after the consignee has generated the Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate (CRAC), payment to the seller is required to be made within:
e: On GeM, after the consignee generates the CRAC, payment to the seller is required to be made within 10 days, keeping marketplace payments prompt.

q: A depot holds 400 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 16 per unit. A fresh receipt of 200 units is taken into stock at Rs 25 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Revised average rate = (400 x Rs 16 + 200 x Rs 25) / 600 units = Rs 11,400 / 600 = Rs 19 per unit.

q: Where stores offered for pre-despatch inspection are rejected by the inspecting authority as not conforming to the specification, the inspection charges incurred on the rejected material are:

options.B: Borne by the Railway in all cases
options.C: Shared equally between the Railway and the supplier
options.D: Adjusted against the earnest money of the supplier

e: Where stores offered for pre-despatch inspection are rejected as not conforming to specification, the inspection charges on the rejected material are recoverable from the supplier who offered non-conforming stores.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 45 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 240 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Shortage value = 45 units x Rs 240 per unit = Rs 10,800, the shortage being valued at the book rate.

q: The Security Deposit required under a stores contract may be furnished by the supplier in the form of:

options.B: Cash deposit, bank guarantee, fixed deposit receipt or recovery from his bills, as stipulated in the contract
options.D: A personal surety bond of two railway employees

e: The Security Deposit may be furnished as cash deposit, bank guarantee, fixed deposit receipt or recovery from the supplier's bills, as stipulated in the contract; it is not confined to cash alone.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 6,00,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 5 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: Liquidated damages = 0.5 per cent of Rs 6,00,000 = Rs 3,000 per week x 5 weeks = Rs 15,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where a supplier fails to replace or repair stores found defective within the warranty period, the Railway may get the defect rectified at the risk and cost of the supplier.
2. The warranty period stipulated in a stores contract can be extended at any time by the depot storekeeper on the request of the supplier.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: if the supplier fails to replace or repair defective stores within the warranty period, the Railway may get the defect rectified at his risk and cost. Statement 2 is false, as a depot storekeeper cannot extend the contractual warranty period.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 40 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 5 crore. The Turnover Ratio of stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance / total issues = Rs 40 lakh / Rs 5 crore = 0.08.

q: In a reverse auction conducted on IREPS for the purchase of stores, the bidding commences from:

options.A: The highest rate received in the tender
options.B: The estimated rate of the item
options.C: The lowest (L1) rate received at the tender stage
options.D: The last accepted rate of the item

e: In a reverse auction on IREPS, bidding commences from the lowest (L1) rate received at the tender stage, and the auction proceeds downward from that rate.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 4,25,000. The advance payment admissible at 98 per cent of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment = 98 per cent of Rs 4,25,000 = Rs 4,16,500, admissible against the inspection certificate and despatch documents.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A separate PL number is allotted to the same stores item by each depot holding it.
2. The PL number of a stores item remains the same in every depot of the railway where the item is stocked.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 2 only is correct: the PL number of an item remains the same in every depot of the railway where it is stocked; it is not allotted separately by each depot, so statement 1 is false.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 1.35 crore, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 3.1 crore and issues during the year are Rs 3.25 crore. The closing balance of stores is:
e: Closing balance = opening Rs 1.35 crore + receipts Rs 3.1 crore - issues Rs 3.25 crore = Rs 1.2 crore.

q: If the AAC (Average Annual Consumption) of a stock item is revised upward, the stock in hand and the dues remaining unchanged, the coverage of the item, expressed in months, will:
e: Coverage in months = (stock in hand + dues) divided by monthly consumption from the AAC, so if the AAC is revised upward with stock and dues unchanged, the same holding covers fewer months and coverage decreases.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 95 lakh and the closing balance is Rs 55 lakh. The average stock held during the year is:
e: Average stock = (opening balance Rs 95 lakh + closing balance Rs 55 lakh) / 2 = Rs 75 lakh.

q: Stores which have been paid for but are still in transit at the close of the financial year are reflected in the stores balance of the railway:

options.A: They are excluded from the stores balance altogether
options.B: Through the debit balance outstanding under Purchase Suspense
options.C: As a liability of the railway
options.D: Through the credit balance under Sales Suspense

e: Stores paid for but still in transit are reflected through the debit balance outstanding under Purchase Suspense, since the bills have been paid but the material has not yet been received into stock.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 1.6 crore and the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 18 per cent per annum of the average stock value. The annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Annual carrying cost = 18 per cent of the average stock value of Rs 1.6 crore = Rs 28.8 lakh.

q: The price charged to a firm for the tender documents of a stores tender is:

options.A: Refunded to the firm if its tender is not accepted
options.B: Adjusted against the earnest money deposit of the firm
options.C: Not refundable, whether or not the firm submits a tender
options.D: Refunded if the tender is discharged without acceptance

e: The price charged for tender documents is a sale price of the documents and is not refundable, whether or not the firm submits a tender or its tender is accepted.

q: The AAC of an item is 4,800 units. The stock in hand is 800 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 200 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Monthly consumption = 4,800 / 12 = 400 units; coverage = (stock in hand 800 + dues 200) / 400 = 2.5 months.

q: Amounts found due to the Railway from a supplier under a stores contract, which cannot be recovered from his bills under that contract, may be recovered from:

options.A: Any sums payable to the supplier under any other contract with the Railway, as provided in the conditions of contract
options.B: The earnest money of other tenderers in the same tender
options.C: The pay of the stores officer who placed the order
options.D: The sale proceeds of scrap held in the depot

e: Amounts due from a supplier that cannot be recovered from his bills under one contract may be recovered from any sums payable to him under any other contract with the Railway, as provided in the conditions of contract.

q: The AAC of an item is 10,200 units. Coverage for three months is required to be provided. The stock in hand is 950 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 450 units. The quantity to be ordered is:
e: Three months' requirement = 10,200 x 3/12 = 2,550 units; quantity to order = 2,550 - stock in hand 950 - dues 450 = 1,150 units.

q: During stock verification, 28 units of an item are found in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 175 per unit. The value of the excess taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account is:
e: Excess value = 28 units x Rs 175 per unit = Rs 4,900, taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: The average consumption of an item is 95 units per week, the lead time for its procurement is 9 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock is 300 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = average consumption x lead time + safety stock = 95 x 9 + 300 = 1,155 units.

q: Stores of a consumable nature, such as oils and paints consumed in use, which are issued from a depot to a consuming department are:

options.A: Required to be returned to the depot after use
options.B: Borne on the Tools and Plant register of the department
options.C: Physically verified in the department every year
options.D: Finally charged off to the consuming head at the time of issue itself, no return being required

e: Consumable stores such as oils and paints are finally charged off to the consuming head at the time of issue itself; being consumed in use, no return to the depot is required.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,850 units. The average consumption is 105 units per week and the average lead time is 10 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum level = re-order level - (average consumption x average lead time) = 1,850 - (105 x 10) = 800 units.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,300 units and the re-order quantity is 950 units. The minimum consumption is 45 units per week and the minimum lead time is 6 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1,300 + 950 - (45 x 6) = 1,980 units.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 260 units per week, its normal consumption is 210 units per week and the lead time is 5 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item is:
e: Safety stock = (maximum consumption - normal consumption) x lead time = (260 - 210) x 5 = 250 units.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A stores item with a very high unit price but negligible annual consumption will necessarily fall in the 'A' category of ABC analysis.
2. A low-priced stores item consumed in very large quantities can fall in the 'A' category, since ABC classification is based on annual consumption value.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 2 only is correct: ABC classification rests on annual consumption value, so a low-priced item consumed in very large quantities can fall in 'A' category; a high-priced item with negligible consumption will not, so statement 1 is false.

q: The minimum level of an item is 1,050 units and the maximum level is 2,450 units. The average stock level of the item is:
e: Average stock level = (minimum level + maximum level) / 2 = (1,050 + 2,450) / 2 = 1,750 units.
